why: Items 4 and 5 mix defending the work against attack with routine watching and repairing, so the T3-005/T3-021 boundary is the hardest to draw.

why.T3-010: The item coordinates borders and space with r/ainbowroad: formalizing the halo, putting the border on their live thread, discussing border size, and reaching out despite pushback. That is settling lines with neighbours, not a fight to end (T3-149) or help sent unasked (T3-011).

The item is a contested placement practice in which the room negotiates sharing space with the Catalan flag (offering to recolor the Puffle, moving negotiation to r/catalunya, arguing recolouring lets everyone get along), rather than a single attack or defence. Confidence arguable because no durable border agreement results.

why.T3-014: All concepts set up a Discord server to communicate, coordinate protection, take on secondary tasks, and choose a template, which is moving the room's planning into a chat.

why.T3-005: The item repeatedly rallies members to protect and defend the start-menu penguin under attack and reports guarding it for hours (C0599897, C0788814, C1411621, C1367585).
why.T3-021: The item's labour also includes cleaning vandals, affirming maintenance, and keeping up general upkeep (C0039593, C0706226, C0871289), which is watching and repairing the work rather than fighting an attack.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-005 alone carries the defence calls but fails to carry the routine cleaning and maintenance labour (cleaning vandals, affirming maintenance, general upkeep), which is not fighting an attack.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: Cleaning vandals, affirming maintenance importance, and asking for general upkeep satisfy T3-021's gate of watching and repairing the work; C0039593 is its distinct support.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-021, because the item's label and strongest concepts are about guarding the penguin; dropping it would lose the maintenance labour but keep the defence core.

why.T3-022: The item's most prominent practice is restarting the penguin at a new location after it was erased by the Mona Lisa or attacked, with many such moves (C0458997, C0496768, C0911262, C1330188, C0580611, C1260048, C0490067, C0247445). Other themes with three or more concepts of their own are T3-005 (C1233167, C1277793, C0450226, C0930946), T3-038 (C1242681, C0950244, C0786958, C1179187), T3-002 (C0545754, C0006993, C0848932, C0617360), and T3-070 (C1411435, C0590051, C0749233).

why.T3-054: The item moves the penguin to other canvas sites and r/PlaceTwo after r/place ended or griefing made the original impossible, reproducing and exchanging the alternative venue (C1385239, C0761343, C0198179, C0472105).

why.T3-031: The exchange is a running joke about the supposed penguin actually being the Linux logo, played in the room's talk.

why.T3-001: The room stages fake Club Penguin comeback claims, marks and exposes them, and plays inside the April Fools fakes (C0177276, C0880913, C0347897, C0905073, C1535673).
why.T3-032: Multiple concepts object to the comeback jokes as horrible, too soon or unwelcome and ask for them to stop (C1483603, C0031123, C0080029, C0931745).

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-001 alone carries the staged fakes and play-along but fails to carry the sustained objection to the jokes (calling them horrible, too soon, asking to stop), which is a distinct practice of objecting rather than making the joke.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: Multiple concepts object to the April Fools comeback jokes as hurtful or stale and ask for them to stop, satisfying T3-032's gate; C1483603 is its distinct support.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-032, because the item's central practice is staging the fake comeback claims; dropping it would lose the objection but keep the fakes.
